title: Hash Tables: Maps, Sets, and Object-Based Storage
description: This module covers one of the most important data structures in computer science: Hash Tables. In JavaScript, hash tables are implemented using objects, Maps, and Sets. They allow for fast lookups, insertions, and deletions — all in constant average time. You’ll learn how hashing works internally, when and how to use plain objects versus Map/Set, and solve common algorithmic problems such as detecting duplicates, counting frequencies, and implementing custom hash functions. Hash tables are not just powerful — they’re everywhere in real-world code, from databases to compilers to caches.

lessons.title: What is a Hash Table?
lessons.content:
A hash table is a data structure that maps keys to values using a hash function. The idea is to transform a key (like a string) into an index in an array using a hash function. This allows constant-time average complexity for insertions, deletions, and lookups. JavaScript provides built-in support for hash tables through `Object`, `Map`, and `Set`.

Basic hash table concepts:
- **Hash function**: Converts a key into a unique index.
- **Collision**: Occurs when two keys hash to the same index.
- **Load factor**: Measures how full the table is (affects resizing).

Real-world examples:
- Storing user sessions
- Implementing dictionaries
- Caching results of expensive function calls

Hash tables are everywhere because they make lookup blazing fast.

Object vs Map vs Set: When to Use What
lessons.content:
**Object**:
- Use when keys are always strings
- Great for static configuration or JSON data

**Map**:
- Better when keys can be any type
- Maintains insertion order
- Ideal for dynamic key-value data

**Set**:
- Use for fast existence checks
- Ideal for unique collections and de-duplication

**Comparison**:
| Feature         | Object | Map  | Set  |
|----------------|--------|------|------|
| Key Types      | String | Any  | Any  |
| Order          | Unordered | Ordered | Ordered |
| Uniqueness     | ❌     | ❌   | ✅   |
| Use Case       | Lookup | Dynamic pairs | Existence testing |

Choose the right tool for the right situation!
